requirements.priority_rationale: Non-interfering background execution is essential for a shared reporting system operating during normal library hours.

requirements.name: Quick Uncataloged Item Distribution
requirements.description: The system shall support rapid distribution workflows for uncataloged Items, including Items received in large shipments. These workflows shall enable staff to process and assign Items for deployment with minimal delay. Acceptance requires that a representative batch of uncataloged Items can be distributed through the workflow without unnecessary per-Item processing steps.
requirements.priority_rationale: Rapid distribution is explicitly requested and is essential to handling incoming uncataloged shipments efficiently.

requirements.name: Minimize Branch Labor
requirements.description: The system shall provide uncataloged Item receiving, tracking, and distribution workflows that minimize Branch staff effort per Item. The workflows shall avoid unnecessary manual steps while preserving the information needed to account for and distribute the Items. Acceptance requires that staff can complete the defined workflow with low and measurable processing effort per Item.
requirements.priority_rationale: Reducing Branch labor is strongly requested and important for operational cost control, although a manual workaround remains possible.

requirements.name: Optional Card Reader Support
requirements.description: The system shall support card-based staff login without requiring card-reader hardware for basic operation. It shall operate at Branches that do not have card readers, using username-and-password authentication where card hardware is unavailable. Deploying or enabling card-reader hardware shall therefore remain optional.
requirements.priority_rationale: The system must remain usable across Branches with differing infrastructure and must not make card-reader installation a prerequisite for operation.

requirements.name: Use Acquisition Dates
requirements.description: The system shall use the existing Item acquisition date field when calculating new acquisitions and historical collection volume. Reports shall rely on the stored acquisition date rather than requiring a separate acquisition-date data source. The field shall support date-based volume calculations.
requirements.priority_rationale: The existing acquisition date is the identified authoritative data source for acquisition and historical volume calculations.

requirements.name: Persist Deletion Audit Records
requirements.description: The system shall capture deletion events through a database trigger that writes an audit record at the time of deletion. The audit records shall be stored in a database audit table. The table shall support reliable querying and aggregation of deletion events. The implementation shall ensure that deletion auditing does not depend on a user remembering to create a separate log entry.
requirements.priority_rationale: The source requirements explicitly mandate database-triggered persistence to make deletion capture reliable.

requirements.name: Adapted Requirements Foundation
requirements.description: The system shall be specified using the King County and Galecia Group draft Software Requirements Specification as a foundation, adapted to the needs of the PINES System. The adapted documentation shall preserve relevant foundation content while incorporating approved PINES-specific requirements. The resulting specification shall be identifiable as the project-specific version used for implementation.
requirements.priority_rationale: The working group explicitly decided to use and adapt the existing specification as the foundation for the project requirements.

requirements.name: Complete Data Specifications
requirements.description: The system shall be accompanied by complete data specifications and data dictionaries for authority, Bibliographic Record, order, Item, Hold, and other records accessed or maintained by Management Processes. The specifications shall identify field names, data types, relationships, and other information needed to construct effective Queries. The documentation shall cover all data exposed to staff for reporting and analysis.
requirements.priority_rationale: Complete data specifications are explicitly demanded as a high-priority foundation for effective Query development.

requirements.name: High-Level Process Documentation
requirements.description: The system shall be accompanied by thorough high-level descriptions of major data and reporting processes. The documentation shall include Bibliographic Record import and export, validation against authority sources, and standard Reports. The descriptions shall explain relevant data flows sufficiently for staff and developers to understand and verify process behaviour.
requirements.priority_rationale: Process documentation is explicitly requested by multiple sources and is important for understanding system behaviour, but core operation can continue with temporary documentation workarounds.

requirements.name: Readable Requirements Specification
requirements.description: The system shall be specified by requirements documentation that is understandable to library managers and staff as well as software project managers and developers. The documentation shall balance readable explanations for non-technical readers with sufficient precision for implementation and verification. Acceptance of the documentation shall be assessed by review from both audience groups.
requirements.priority_rationale: The working group explicitly identifies both managerial and development audiences, making readable yet precise documentation important for successful implementation.

requirements.name: Library Terminology Assumption
requirements.description: The system shall be documented for readers who are assumed to understand common library services and processes. The requirements documentation need not define established library terminology, but it shall provide definitions for project-specific terms, ambiguous concepts, and technical details needed for implementation or verification. Documentation reviews shall confirm that omitted definitions do not prevent the intended audiences from interpreting requirements.
requirements.priority_rationale: This is an explicitly recorded documentation convention with limited operational impact and can be supplemented by a glossary or reviewer clarification when needed.

requirements.name: Defer Detailed Interface Specification
requirements.description: The system shall defer detailed user-interface and data-structure specifications during the initial requirements phase. The project shall prioritize documenting functional requirements before completing those specifications. The project shall refine the deferred specifications later through iterative prototyping.
requirements.priority_rationale: The source explicitly states that detailed interface and data-structure specification is deferred until a later phase.

requirements.name: Meet Financial Audit Requirements
requirements.description: The system shall produce financial Reports and preserve financial data in accordance with applicable accounting practices and state, county, and municipal auditing requirements. Compliance shall apply to both generated Reports and archived financial data. The resulting records shall support review and audit of financial activity.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accounting and audit compliance is an explicit legal and operational obligation.

requirements.name: Retain Financial Transaction History
requirements.description: The system shall retain detailed financial Transaction history for the period required by applicable law and audit practice, with the retention period configurable by authorized administrators where permitted. The system shall support a legally specified period such as seven years rather than imposing a shorter fixed period. Monthly and annual aggregate transaction information shall be retained indefinitely for reporting and compliance.
requirements.priority_rationale: Legally required financial retention and indefinite aggregate retention are necessary for audit compliance and longitudinal reporting.

requirements.name: Reuse Existing Query Builder
requirements.description: The system shall integrate transfer candidate selection with the existing Query builder. Transfer staff shall be able to use the builder's supported criteria and selection capabilities without maintaining a separate transfer-only query mechanism. Acceptance shall include creating or running a transfer Query through the existing builder and passing its results to the transfer workflow.
requirements.priority_rationale: Reusing the existing Query builder reduces duplicate functionality and implementation effort while preserving the required selection capability.

requirements.name: Supported Web Browsers
requirements.description: The system shall support browser-based access through Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6.0 and later and Mozilla Firefox version 2.0 and later when web-browser access is used. Supported browser operation shall include the reporting functions available to the user. Acceptance shall verify access and execution of the relevant reporting workflows in each specified browser family and version range.
requirements.priority_rationale: Browser compatibility is an explicit library standard and is needed for practical access to the reporting system.

requirements.name: Qualifying Activity Calculation
requirements.description: The system shall determine each Patron's most recent qualifying activity from Circulation and electronic activity sources. Electronic activity shall include OPAC or Patron account logins, online Hold placement, online renewals, and digital collection access when integrated. The system shall combine activity stored in separate source tables and use the resulting latest activity date to apply the Inactivity threshold. The calculation shall be based on recorded Transactions or activity records rather than a manually maintained status.
requirements.priority_rationale: Accurate identification of inactivity depends on combining all specified activity sources and applying the threshold consistently.

requirements.name: Calculate Age From Birthdate
requirements.description: The system shall calculate a Patron's age from the recorded birthdate when evaluating an age range. The calculation shall occur at Query or Report execution time so that age grouping reflects the current date. The system shall use the calculated age rather than relying on a permanently stored age value.
requirements.priority_rationale: Current age grouping requires a consistent calculation from the authoritative birthdate field.

requirements.name: CSV Report Export
requirements.description: The system shall allow the inactive Patron Report to be exported in CSV format. The exported file shall contain the selected Report fields and records in a machine-readable structure suitable for outreach or third-party processing. Export shall respect the Report's filters and exclusions.
requirements.priority_rationale: CSV export is explicitly requested to support operational outreach and integration with external tools.

requirements.name: Enterprise Infrastructure Compatibility
requirements.description: The system shall operate within the enterprise infrastructure supporting the Library Automation System. It may rely on available redundant servers, backup systems, and network connectivity rather than independently replacing those services. Acceptance shall verify deployment and operation using the supported enterprise infrastructure.
requirements.priority_rationale: Compatibility with the existing resilient infrastructure is necessary for deployment and operational continuity.

requirements.name: Enterprise Library System Integration
requirements.description: The system shall operate as an integrated component of an enterprise-level Library Automation System. It shall use and remain compatible with the enterprise system's general data structures and functionality rather than assuming an independent data model. Acceptance shall verify interoperability with the target enterprise services and data structures.
requirements.priority_rationale: Integration with the existing enterprise Library Automation System is required for the system to function in its target environment.

requirements.name: Normalized Relational Reporting
requirements.description: The system shall execute reporting against the primary normalized relational database schema without requiring a separately maintained denormalized reporting schema or synchronized copy. Queries shall support complex joins across relevant relational data while treating the operational relational schema as authoritative. Acceptance shall verify that required Reports use the normalized schema, support representative complex joins, and do not depend on denormalized synchronization.
requirements.priority_rationale: The sources explicitly require reliable reporting against the authoritative relational schema while avoiding synchronization problems from denormalized copies.

requirements.name: Patron-Facing Scope Boundary
requirements.description: The system shall exclude day-to-day Patron-facing functions from its scope. Those functions shall remain the responsibility of the OPAC and circulation client rather than being implemented in the reporting system. Acceptance shall verify that the delivered system provides staff reporting capabilities without claiming responsibility for routine Patron-facing transactions.
requirements.priority_rationale: The stakeholder explicitly defines this boundary to prevent overlap with the OPAC and circulation client.

requirements.name: PostgreSQL Platform Compatibility
requirements.description: The system shall be compatible with the PostgreSQL database platform used by PINES. It shall operate against the existing production database environment, including the currently identified PostgreSQL 8.3 platform where applicable. Acceptance shall verify deployment and reporting against the supported PostgreSQL environment.
requirements.priority_rationale: Compatibility with the existing PostgreSQL platform is required for deployment in the target environment.

requirements.name: Preserve OPAC Independence
requirements.description: The system shall remain separate from the OPAC and shall not constrain, alter, or require changes to OPAC functionality or features. Management and reporting capabilities shall not impose dependencies that reduce the OPAC's autonomy. Verification shall confirm that reporting changes can be deployed without modifying public-facing OPAC behavior.
requirements.priority_rationale: Multiple meeting records state that the reporting system must not constrain the public catalog, including an explicit statement that this is unacceptable.

requirements.name: Production Reporting Isolation
requirements.description: The system shall separate reporting workloads from production operational processing so reporting Queries do not adversely affect transactional performance. It shall support a separate reporting database or a read-only reporting replica when required to offload reporting Queries from the primary database. Acceptance shall verify that reporting can execute through the separated architecture without directly burdening production operations.
requirements.priority_rationale: Protecting production transaction performance is essential for a system that shares infrastructure with operational services.

requirements.name: Relational Database Backend
requirements.description: The system shall use a fully relational database backend for storing and retrieving reporting data. Reporting and Query processing shall operate correctly against the relational data model used by the Library Automation System. Acceptance shall verify that required reporting functions work with the existing relational structure.
requirements.priority_rationale: A relational backend is explicitly required and is essential for compatibility with the existing Library Automation System data model.

requirements.name: Run On Existing Hardware
requirements.description: The system shall run acceptably on the existing central IT server class used by PINES. The target environment includes Red Hat Enterprise Linux 5 with dual quad-core processors and 32 GB of RAM. Deployment verification shall demonstrate supported operation and acceptable performance on that server class.
requirements.priority_rationale: Compatibility with the existing central infrastructure is necessary for deployment without an immediate hardware replacement.

requirements.name: Separated Development Training Environments
requirements.description: The system shall provide separate development, training, and production environments for report development, staff practice, and live operation. It shall support exporting and importing report Templates, permission settings, and other configuration from development or training into production. Acceptance shall verify that configuration can be migrated without directly modifying production during development or training activities.
requirements.priority_rationale: Separate environments and controlled configuration migration are repeatedly required to protect live operations and support safe deployment.

requirements.name: Standards-Compliant HTML Output
requirements.description: The system shall produce standards-compliant HTML for web interfaces, Reports, and help content. The HTML shall validate against applicable W3C standards and use semantic structure, including alternative text and appropriate ARIA labels where needed. Output shall remain interoperable across supported browsers and assistive technologies.
requirements.priority_rationale: Standards-compliant and accessible HTML is explicitly marked high priority and is required across the system's web output.

requirements.name: Supported Client Access
requirements.description: The system shall provide staff access to reporting functionality through at least one supported client environment: a web browser or a Windows-compatible client. The implementation shall document which option is supported and shall not require both client environments for acceptance. Acceptance shall demonstrate complete Report access and execution through the selected supported option.
requirements.priority_rationale: Client access is an explicitly stated deployment requirement, while the source wording permits either client environment.

requirements.name: Supported Server Platforms
requirements.description: The system shall be deployable and operational on both Linux, including Red Hat Enterprise Linux, and Solaris 10 on SPARC server environments. Deployment documentation shall identify the supported configurations for both operating-system families. Acceptance shall verify installation, startup, and Report execution on each required platform.
requirements.priority_rationale: The sources explicitly require both server operating-system families for primary and secondary deployment environments.

requirements.name: Use Enterprise ILS Data
requirements.description: The system shall rely on and interoperate with the enterprise ILS data structures and supported functionality, including Acquisitions and Cataloging data. It shall read and query this data for management Reports and related operations. It shall not manage or modify Acquisitions or Cataloging functions.
requirements.priority_rationale: The system depends on the enterprise ILS as the authoritative source for core Acquisitions and Cataloging data.

requirements.name: Disaster Recovery Site Operation
requirements.description: The system shall support operation at the secondary disaster recovery site running Solaris 10 on SPARC. Reporting and applicable recovery processes shall remain available when deployed at that site. Acceptance shall verify installation and execution at the secondary site using its available infrastructure.
requirements.priority_rationale: Secondary-site operation is important for resilience and recovery, although routine operations can continue at the primary site.

requirements.name: Transit Detection Logic
requirements.description: The system shall identify an Item as overdue in Transit when its Transit record has no arrival date and its departure date is older than the configured Transit threshold. The detection shall use the applicable Transit data records as the source of departure and arrival information. Items meeting these conditions shall be eligible for the overdue Transit Report.
requirements.priority_rationale: The specified detection rule provides a concrete and consistent basis for overdue Transit reporting, although it is an implementation constraint rather than a user-facing core feature.

blacklist.name: Investigate Technical Constraints
blacklist.description: A technical investigation must be performed to identify feasibility constraints before building the interface.
blacklist.explanation: This is a project activity rather than behavior required of the software. The resulting technical constraints may inform requirements, but conducting the investigation is not itself a system requirement.

blacklist.name: Produce Initial Mockups
blacklist.description: Initial mockups or visual designs of the capacity interface must be produced as project deliverables.
blacklist.explanation: Producing initial mockups is a design and project deliverable, not a required runtime capability of the software. Interface behavior is captured by the retained Branch capacity requirements.

blacklist.name: Careful Technical Design Required
blacklist.description: The transfer utility requires careful system design and technical investigation.
blacklist.explanation: This candidate describes a project planning or engineering activity rather than observable software behavior or a testable system constraint. Its concerns are addressed by the functional and scalability requirements instead.

blacklist.name: Support Extensive Batch Operations
blacklist.description: The system must support extensive batch operations across cataloging functions, including queries, transfers, status changes, and deletions.
blacklist.explanation: The statement is not measurable and bundles several distinct capabilities, including transfers and queries, without defining the required operations, limits, or acceptance criteria. Its purge-related portions are covered by the specific batch requirements.

blacklist.name: Reports Testing Group Workflow
blacklist.description: All new Reports development shall be filtered through the Reports testing group before wider deployment.
blacklist.explanation: These candidates specify a project or release-governance process rather than behavior required of the Report software. The process may be documented elsewhere, but it is not a Report Operations system requirement.

blacklist.name: Requirement Gathering Interviews
blacklist.description: Each working group member shall conduct an interview with staff at their library system to gather Report needs by a specified date.
blacklist.explanation: This is a project action and meeting follow-up, not a requirement on the software. The interview deadline and participant obligations belong in project planning documentation.

blacklist.name: Streamlined Login Improves Security
blacklist.description: The streamlined login method should improve security compared to manual credential entry by reducing password sharing and unattended logged-in terminals.
blacklist.explanation: The candidate states an unmeasurable comparative outcome without defining a security metric, threat model, or acceptance threshold. The concrete security controls are captured by the requirements for individual card authentication, login auditing, and unattended session protection.

blacklist.name: Architectural Constraints Meeting
blacklist.description: A technical subcommittee must meet to identify and discuss architectural constraints affecting the reporting system.
blacklist.explanation: This candidate specifies a meeting and project activity rather than behavior, quality, or constraint of the software.

blacklist.name: Iterative Prototype Development
blacklist.description: Development of Reports and the user interface must follow a collaborative, iterative, prototype-oriented methodology.
blacklist.explanation: This specifies a project development process rather than behavior or a quality constraint of the deployed software.

blacklist.name: Unavailable Configuration Migration
blacklist.description: Configuration migration between development, testing, and production environments is not available.
blacklist.explanation: This contradicts the later technical-subcommittee requirement to provide configuration migration, including export and import of Templates, permissions, and saved Queries. The later requirement is retained as "Migrate Environment Configuration".

blacklist.name: Unavailable Real-Time Reporting
blacklist.description: Real-time reporting is not available and all Reports run only on current data.
blacklist.explanation: This conflicts with the stakeholder survey request for real-time or near-real-time reporting for operational monitoring. The retained requirement is "Real-Time Reporting Capability".

blacklist.name: Limit SRS To Management Activities
blacklist.description: The requirements specification should include only requirements directly or indirectly related to management activities.
blacklist.explanation: This is a documentation-scoping decision for the requirements process, not a behavior, quality, or implementation constraint of the software.

blacklist.name: Immediate Badge Login
blacklist.description: The system shall log a staff member in immediately after a successful badge swipe without requiring another credential.
blacklist.explanation: This candidate conflicts with the kept authentication policy that a badge identifies the staff account but does not bypass individual authentication or a required second credential.

issues.description: FR-002 says a successful badge swipe authenticates staff without additional credentials, while FR-004 says badge use must not bypass individual authentication. These statements leave unclear whether the badge alone is an acceptable individual credential.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify whether a mapped badge swipe is itself sufficient individual authentication or whether a second credential is required, then align both requirements and their acceptance criteria.

issues.description: CON-013 says access may be through either a browser or a Windows-compatible client and that acceptance need only demonstrate one option, but it also requires compatibility with both declared client environments.
issues.suggested_fix: State explicitly whether both client environments are mandatory or whether either one is sufficient, and make the acceptance criteria consistent with that choice.

issues.description: The exclusion of Patron-facing functions is a valid scope boundary: it clarifies that those functions remain with the OPAC and circulation client and prevents ambiguity about what this System must provide. Treating it as out of scope for the requirements document does not explain why the scope need should be lost.
issues.suggested_fix: Restore this as a scope constraint stating that the System does not provide day-to-day Patron-facing functions, which remain the responsibility of the OPAC and circulation client.

issues.description: Both requirements require a system-wide overview of capacity for all Branches, with aggregation across Branches and an overview or dashboard presentation. They describe substantially the same capability.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge the requirements, retaining the all-Branch overview, centralized aggregation, and high-level capacity metrics in one testable requirement.

issues.description: Both requirements require selected MARC values to be extracted and presented in one row per Bibliographic Record. Their core behavior and acceptance conditions are the same.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge into one requirement covering selected MARC-field extraction, record association, and single-row output, with a clear rule for repeated values.

issues.description: FR-181 and NFR-025 both require Report processing through background execution or a queue without blocking normal operations. NFR-025 adds open-hours and Circulation-client performance expectations, but the central background-processing need is repeated.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate the shared background-processing requirement while retaining the queue behavior, open-hours operation, and measurable non-interference criteria in the consolidated requirement.

issues.description: FR-006's required data-quality Report conditions overlap with the specific Reports in FR-011, FR-110, and FR-120; its no-associated-Items condition also overlaps FR-097. The additional periodic behavior in some specific requirements does not distinguish the shared detection and reporting capability.
issues.suggested_fix: Define whether FR-006 is a suite or an umbrella requirement. Avoid requiring the same report output twice, and keep any genuinely distinct periodic execution behavior explicit in the specific requirements.

issues.description: FR-012 bundles several distinct Report needs: added and edited counts, total counts, lists of added Items, and standard deleted, checked-out, overdue, and missing-status Reports. The merged description makes them a single suite but does not give each distinct Report a separately verifiable requirement or clear acceptance condition.
issues.suggested_fix: Split the suite into separately testable requirements, or enumerate each required Report and its acceptance criteria explicitly so none can be considered satisfied by only part of the suite.

issues.description: Both requirements address Linux/Solaris deployment, but CON-012 allows deployment on at least one of the two platform families while CON-022 requires Linux and Solaris 10 on SPARC. The overlapping requirements leave the intended support obligation unclear.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace both with one explicit platform requirement that states whether Linux, Solaris, or both are required and identifies the required versions and configurations.

issues.description: Both requirements require reporting against the normalized relational schema without a separately maintained denormalized schema. CON-031 adds support for complex joins, which is a distinct detail but does not justify repeating the shared schema constraint.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate the normalized-schema constraint and retain complex-join support as an explicit additional condition in the consolidated requirement.

issues.description: These requirements describe general planning, evaluation, and management reporting needs without specifying the operational or program metrics, report outputs, or other criteria that would establish whether the capability is complete. Their scopes also substantially overlap.
issues.suggested_fix: Identify the intended stakeholder roles and required report types or metrics, and clarify whether these are distinct from the specific analytics requirements or should be consolidated with them.

issues.description: The requirement permits either integration with WorldCat or 'direct assistance for accessing' records, without defining the required system behavior or what assistance must be provided. Its acceptance criteria therefore cannot establish conformance.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify the required interaction, such as launching or displaying WorldCat records for a last-copy Item, and define how the system supports cataloger review without implying unbounded editing functionality.

issues.description: These requirements use 'copy' or 'copies' for the cataloged physical entity, although the glossary specifies Item as the preferred term replacing copy. This can make the scope of last-copy checks unclear.
issues.suggested_fix: Use Item consistently and specify whether each sole-Item or last-copy check is per title, Branch, or System.

review_history.summary: Several material issues remain, including an authentication contradiction, inconsistent client-platform obligations, duplicated reporting capabilities, and a bundled Item Report suite that is not independently verifiable. The scope exclusion for Patron-facing functions should also be retained as a valid boundary; the remaining wording and terminology issues should be clarified before approval.

issues.description: FR-001 says a mapped badge is sufficient authentication and logs the staff member in without another credential, while D13-C07 says a card must not bypass authentication. These statements may require opposite login behavior.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify whether badge possession alone is an approved authentication factor or whether a second credential is required, then revise FR-001 and its merged candidate set to state one testable policy.

issues.description: Both requirements specify a material-volume Report for a selected Branch or System. FR-046 adds the breakdown of total, new, on-shelf, and checked-out Items, while FR-045 adds an as-of date and governance use; these appear to be facets of one Report rather than separate capabilities.
issues.suggested_fix: Combine the requirements into one material-volume Report specification that includes the required counts, scope, as-of/date behavior, and reporting purpose.

issues.description: FR-048 and CON-002 both require estimating Shelf Space because it is not directly tracked, including use of estimates or proxy values. The same capability is stated as both a functional requirement and a constraint.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate the estimation behavior in one requirement and retain any separate implementation constraint only if it adds a distinct, necessary restriction.

issues.description: Both requirements cover emailing generated Reports to specified recipients, including scheduled delivery. FR-209 additionally covers on-demand delivery and output format; FR-237 adds identifying delivery failures.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge these into one email-delivery requirement that preserves on-demand and scheduled delivery, recipient selection, supported formats, and delivery-failure reporting.

issues.description: FR-009 requires a Report of Bibliographic Records without associated volumes or Items, and FR-010 includes that same condition in its data-quality suite. The same reporting need is stated twice.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify whether the no-Items check is a standalone Report, a component of the data-quality suite, or both; avoid duplicating the requirement while preserving any distinct execution or presentation behavior.

issues.description: Both requirements require staff to track and manage uncataloged materials as inventory before a full Bibliographic Record exists. FR-255 adds acceptance detail, but the core capability is duplicated.
issues.suggested_fix: Combine these requirements, retaining FR-255's requirements to record, locate, manage, and report an uncataloged Item without a completed Bibliographic Record.

issues.description: Both requirements cover reporting use of uncataloged materials. FR-256 adds the specific monthly in-house-use measure, but FR-114's general usage reporting overlaps that capability.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate the uncataloged-use requirements and explicitly retain monthly in-house-use counts and any other distinct usage measures.

issues.description: FR-100 requires uncataloged Item Transactions to be included in overall Circulation statistics and Reports; FR-115 requires counting those Transactions in Circulation statistics and Reports. The principal behavior is the same.
issues.suggested_fix: Merge these requirements, stating whether uncataloged Transactions must be included in existing totals, separately identifiable, or both.

issues.description: FR-145 provides Patron counts by county, city, and ZIP code, which includes the county-only count required by FR-144. The narrower county requirement is redundant unless it requires a distinct Report or behavior.
issues.suggested_fix: Combine the geographic count requirements and preserve a county-only view as a supported grouping if it is needed independently.

issues.description: Both NFRs require Reports or searches to operate during open hours without disrupting routine circulation or other production services. NFR-017 covers OPAC responsiveness as well, but the non-disruption requirement is substantially repeated.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate the shared availability/performance requirement, explicitly listing circulation-client, OPAC, and other protected workflows and the relevant acceptance conditions.

issues.description: Both requirements specify visible Report execution states, including queued/waiting, processing/running, completed, and failed. FR-235 adds queue position and submission details, but the status behavior is duplicated.
issues.suggested_fix: Define the processing states once in the Report Queue requirement and have the processing-status requirement refer to that shared state model, or remove the redundant requirement.

issues.description: D12-C31 includes preempting Reports, but FR-238 only requires priority-based ordering of waiting jobs. It does not cover interrupting or preempting a lower-priority Report that is already running.
issues.suggested_fix: Confirm whether running Reports must be preemptible. If so, specify the conditions, authorization, and handling of a preempted Report; otherwise remove preemption from the candidate scope.

issues.description: D10-C60 specifies a periodic Last Copy Report, but FR-102 only requires that the Report be provided. Its description does not require periodic or scheduled execution.
issues.suggested_fix: Add the required recurring execution behavior and scheduling options to FR-102, or clarify that periodic execution is not required and should not be included in the merged candidate.

issues.description: D10-C59 specifies a periodic Report of Items in Transit over the threshold, while FR-246 only requires generating a Report. The periodic execution need is not covered.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify whether the overdue Transit Report must run periodically; if it must, state the scheduling or recurrence behavior in FR-246.

issues.description: D14-C44 calls for maintaining Bills Canned Reports, but FR-075 names only Bills Currently Owed, Detailed Payments Received, and Aged Debt. If D14-C44 includes other maintained Bills Canned Reports, those needs are not identified.
issues.suggested_fix: Enumerate the required Bills Canned Reports represented by D14-C44, or narrow that candidate to the three Reports already specified in FR-075.

issues.description: The glossary standardizes the concept as Audit Log and says it replaces “audit table” and “audit trail.” CON-004 uses “audit table,” and NFR-022's title uses “Audit Trail,” although its description uses Audit Log.
issues.suggested_fix: Use Audit Log consistently for the retained record. If CON-004 intentionally mandates a database table as an implementation constraint, distinguish that physical storage detail from the user-facing Audit Log terminology.

issues.description: The glossary standardizes “copy” as Item, but these requirements use “last copy” and “sole-copy” language without consistently naming the counted entity as an Item.
issues.suggested_fix: Use Item consistently in the requirement text, while defining “last Item” or “sole Item” conditions clearly at the title/Bibliographic Record and Branch or System scope.

issues.description: “Acceptable response times” and “excessively delayed” are not testable thresholds. The requirement says targets shall be defined, but it does not provide those targets or identify the Reports and load conditions they apply to.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify response-time targets for representative Reports, along with peak workload, data volume, and measurement conditions.

issues.description: The requirement refers broadly to “relevant operational or program metrics” and management objectives without identifying the required Reports or metrics. This makes implementation and acceptance difficult to verify.
issues.suggested_fix: List the required planning and evaluation metrics or reference a controlled, approved catalog of manager Reports and their acceptance criteria.

review_history.summary: Several retained requirements repeat the same reporting capabilities, particularly for material volume, uncataloged Items, email delivery, processing status, and operational availability. There are also specific merged needs that are not carried through, including periodic execution and Report preemption, plus a contradictory badge-authentication statement. No automatic validator findings were provided; major issues remain, so the requirements are not approved.

issues.description: CON-019 requires reporting against the primary normalized database and disallows a synchronized copy, while CON-023 permits a separate reporting database or read-only replica, and FR-174 calls for a reporting warehouse or equivalent historical store. NFR-016 and NFR-024 also require reporting isolation and background processing, which may depend on the separated architecture. These requirements do not establish which architecture is permitted.
issues.suggested_fix: Choose and state a consistent architecture policy. For example, permit a read-only replica or historical warehouse while requiring it to remain relational and synchronized, and revise CON-019 to prohibit only unnecessary denormalization rather than any synchronized copy. Align NFR-016, NFR-024, CON-023, and FR-174 with that policy.

issues.description: FR-016 requires a Patron count Canned Report grouped by home Branch, and FR-149 separately requires counts of Patrons grouped by home Branch. Both specify the same report capability; the canned-report aspect does not make the underlying count a distinct need.
issues.suggested_fix: Consolidate the Branch-level count into one requirement, explicitly stating whether it must be a maintained Canned Report. Retain FR-016's total Patron count requirement if it is not covered elsewhere.

issues.description: Candidate D14-C09 calls for access to full database fields. FR-189 says to expose relevant available fields and gives Item examples, but it does not clearly require the full reportable schema to be available. The qualifier “relevant” leaves room to omit fields that the candidate explicitly requested.
issues.suggested_fix: State whether all fields in the approved reportable schema must be available for Query and Report authoring, subject to permissions. If so, say so explicitly and define how custom and advanced fields are included.

issues.description: D04-C03 includes sharing saved Queries, but FR-199 only requires saving and reusing definitions. FR-226 covers shared folders for Reports and Templates, not explicitly sharing Query definitions, so the candidate's sharing need is not clearly covered.
issues.suggested_fix: Add an explicit requirement to share saved Query definitions with authorized users or groups, or extend FR-226 to include Queries and identify how Query permissions are controlled.

issues.description: The candidates request a list of Patrons with an inactive status, while FR-159 defines the result solely by absence of qualifying activity during an Inactivity period. A Patron's recorded inactive status may not be equivalent to that activity calculation, so reporting the status-based population is not assured.
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify whether the Report must include Patrons whose account status is inactive, independently of the activity-based Inactivity rule. If required, add that status as a selectable criterion or a separate Report result condition.

issues.description: The NFR-021 title uses “Audit Trail,” although the glossary specifies “Audit Log” as the standard term and says it replaces “audit trail.” The description itself uses “Audit Log,” making the terminology inconsistent within the requirement.
issues.suggested_fix: Rename NFR-021 to “Record Purge Audit Log” and use “Audit Log” consistently.

issues.description: FR-053 uses “Home Library,” while the glossary standardizes this concept as “Branch.” The same requirement uses “Branch” elsewhere, which makes the grouping terminology inconsistent.
issues.suggested_fix: Replace “Home Library” with “home Branch” in FR-053 and use the glossary term consistently.

issues.description: NFR-020 requires Reports to meet “acceptable response times” but provides no response-time thresholds. It says targets will be defined, leaving the performance requirement untestable until those targets are supplied.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify response-time targets for representative Report types, workload conditions, and data volumes, including the measurement method and acceptable failure rate.

review_history.summary: The requirements contain a significant architecture conflict between direct reporting on the primary database and the use of replicas or a reporting warehouse. Several merged needs also remain uncovered or are duplicated, particularly Query sharing, full-field access, inactive-status reporting, and Patron counts by Branch. Resolve the major issues before approval.
